summary: Isomer's UniformTypeIdentifiers is `UTType` as SwiftUI's pickers take it: a kind of content (`allowedContentTypes: [.image, .pdf]`), its identifier, and the MIME type and file extension a host filters by, for the common types (images, movies, audio, PDF, text, JSON, HTML, ZIP). An app imports it to name `UTType`, as on Apple platforms. On Apple platforms an app uses Apple's.
deviations: A type is its identifier and MIME type: there is no type registry or conformance tree, so `UTType(_:)` knows the common identifiers and `UTType(mimeType:)` / `UTType(filenameExtension:)` the common MIME types and extensions, and other identifiers are dynamic types with no MIME type.

groups.title: Conformance and the type tree
groups.why: `conforms(to:)`, `supertypes`, `isSubtype(of:)`, and the declared/dynamic/public queries, which need a table of the system's types and how they relate. The pickers filter by MIME type, which needs none of it; apps that sort files by kind do.

groups.title: More system types
groups.why: The rest of the system's named types (`UTType.swiftSource`, `.rtf`, `.mp3`, …): each is a constant with its MIME type and extension, added as apps name them.

groups.title: Objective-C bridging and declared equality
groups.why: `UTType.ReferenceType` (the bridge to `UTTypeReference`) and the `==` Apple declares (Isomer's is the synthesized one of a Hashable struct).

groups.title: Tags and references
groups.why: `UTTagClass` and `UTTypeReference` (the Objective-C bridge's reference type): the tags are the MIME type and extension `UTType` already has.

groups.title: Foundation extensions
groups.why: Paths with a type's extension (`URL.appendingPathExtension(for:)`) and a file's type (`URLResourceValues.contentType`); Isomer's Foundation has URL but not resource values.

groups.title: NSItemProvider
groups.why: `NSItemProvider` is an Objective-C class of Foundation's; Isomer's Foundation has no Objective-C classes.

additions: Isomer's UniformTypeIdentifiers declares nothing Apple's lacks; anything listed here is a regression.
